stem: An 8-day-old girl has had vomiting, jaundice and an enlarged liver since milk feeds began, and red-cell galactose-1-phosphate uridyltransferase activity was found to be very low. She now has fever and cool, mottled skin with a blood pressure of 52/30 mm Hg. Blood culture grows indole-positive gram-negative rods.
oneliner: 8-day-old girl + milk-onset jaundice and hepatomegaly + low red-cell GALT + new fever and shock + indole-positive gram-negative rods in blood → organism?
ask: Which organism most likely grew in her blood?

whyNot.A: **Gram-positive cocci** in chains; the blood culture shows **gram-negative rods**
whyNot.B: A gram-**positive** rod; the culture shows **gram-negative** rods
whyNot.C: A gram-**positive** coccus in clusters; the culture shows **gram-negative rods**
whyNot.E: Also a gram-negative rod, but **indole negative**, and it is **not the organism tied to galactosemia**

why: Infants with **classic galactosemia** are prone to **E. coli sepsis** in the first weeks of life, probably because **galactose metabolites impair neutrophil killing**. The **gram-negative rods** in this baby fit **E. coli**.

bug.name: Escherichia coli
bug.lab: Lactose fermenter (pink on MacConkey, green metallic sheen on EMB), indole positive, oxidase negative
bug.virulence: K1 capsule (neonatal meningitis), LPS endotoxin, fimbriae for adhesion, heat-labile and heat-stable toxins in ETEC, Shiga-like toxin in EHEC
bug.spread: Fecal-oral, maternal birth canal at delivery, ascending infection of the urinary tract
bug.causes: UTI, neonatal sepsis and meningitis, traveler diarrhea, hemolytic uremic syndrome (O157:H7), cholecystitis, peritonitis

idea.rule: Galactosemia in a newborn who suddenly deteriorates means gram-negative (E. coli) sepsis until proven otherwise.
also: E. coli is also the commonest cause of neonatal meningitis with K1 capsule and of UTI
Group B Streptococcus: commonest neonatal sepsis overall
Listeria: maternal contact with unpasteurized foods
Removing galactose from feeds lowers the sepsis risk along with liver damage
